statement: At a single observational follow-up visit (MPLONG), as described in the FDA's briefing document (its own analyses of the sponsor's data; the published trial reports give no outcome after 18 weeks), held 6 months to more than 2 years after treatment (median 23.4 months after the last session for MAPP1 participants, 8.5 months for MAPP2), the 137 phase 3 participants who enrolled and were assessed (56 of 91 randomized in MAPP1, 81 of 104 in MAPP2) still showed a difference between the original arms: CAPS-5 had fallen from baseline by 30.3 vs 15.6 points (MAPP1) and 28.0 vs 16.1 points (MAPP2), differences of 14.7 and 12.0 points that the FDA reports without intervals; from week 18 to the visit the MDMA arms improved by a further 5.5 (95% CI 1.1 to 10.0) and 3.6 (1.1 to 6.1) points, and the placebo arms changed little (+0.3 and -0.7). The FDA judged that the follow-up was not designed to evaluate durability: it had no prespecified analysis or error control; enrolment was voluntary and those who enrolled had done better by the end of the trials (CAPS-5 20.2 vs 30.9); MAPP1 participants knew their allocation before the visit; in the interval most participants had other psychotherapy, 12 had ketamine-assisted therapy, and 13 people from the MDMA arms and 7 from the placebo arms reported taking MDMA obtained outside the study; and when the FDA set aside scores after such drug use, the further improvement on MDMA was no longer distinguishable from zero in MAPP2 (-2.0, 95% CI -4.6 to 0.6), though it remained in MAPP1 (-4.9, -9.3 to -0.5) until the imputed scores were penalized. Many members of the FDA's advisory committee found the follow-up too confounded to judge durability. Whether the benefit of MDMA-assisted therapy over placebo with the same therapy lasts beyond 18 weeks is therefore not established. Certainty: very low. Status: single study.
plain: Months to years after the trials, people who had MDMA still had lower PTSD scores than people who had the dummy pill. But only about 7 in 10 people came back for this one check, those who came back had done better, people from the first trial knew which pill they had had, and many had other treatments in between, some of them MDMA from outside the study. The US regulator said this check was not designed to show whether the benefit lasts.
population: Adults with PTSD from the two phase 3 trials (MAPP1, MAPP2) who enrolled in the observational follow-up study MPLONG and were assessed (137 of 195 randomized)
exposure: MDMA in three sessions within the trials' manualized therapy, with no further doses in the study
comparator: Placebo with the same therapy (the original randomized arm)
outcome: CAPS-5 total severity at a single follow-up visit 6 months to more than 2 years after the parent trial, and its change from week 18
magnitude: Effectiveness subset (FDA Table 8): least-squares mean change in CAPS-5 from parent-trial baseline at the follow-up visit, MAPP1 -30.31 on MDMA (n = 27) vs -15.61 on placebo (n = 29), MAPP2 -28.01 (n = 44) vs -16.05 (n = 37); between-arm differences -14.7 and -11.96 (FDA, no interval); at week 18 in the same subsets -8.8 and -9.0 (editors' calculation from Table 8). Change from week 18 to the visit: -5.51 (95% CI -9.95 to -1.07) and -3.60 (-6.10 to -1.09) on MDMA, +0.34 (-3.90 to 4.59) and -0.69 (-3.43 to 2.05) on placebo. FDA tipping-point analysis (scores after interim ketamine, 5-MeO-DMT or MDMA use treated as missing, mITT): -2.02 (-4.61 to 0.57) in MAPP2 and -4.93 (-9.32 to -0.53) in MAPP1 at no penalty. Attendance 56 of 91 and 81 of 104 randomized; median interval 23.4 (7.9 to 32.4) and 8.5 (6.0 to 22.8) months after the last treatment.

evidence.extracted: MPLONG effectiveness subset: least-squares mean CAPS-5 change from parent baseline at week 18 and at the follow-up visit, MAPP1 MDMA (n 27) -24.80 then -30.31, placebo (n 29) -15.96 then -15.61; MAPP2 MDMA (n 44) -24.41 then -28.01, placebo (n 37) -15.36 then -16.05; change from week 18 to the visit -5.51 (95% CI -9.95 to -1.07) and +0.34 (-3.90 to 4.59) in MAPP1, -3.60 (-6.10 to -1.09) and -0.69 (-3.43 to 2.05) in MAPP2. Editors' calculation: between-arm differences of least-squares means 8.8 and 9.0 at week 18 in these subsets.

evidence.locator: Benefit-Risk Framework, Benefits row, Evidence and Uncertainties column, 5th bullet
evidence.extracted: MPLONG assessed 60 participants from MAPP1 (unblinded) and 82 from MAPP2 (still blinded) once, at least 6 months later; a similar difference from placebo was maintained (-14.7 in MAPP1 and -11.96 in MAPP2) with continued improvement from week 18 in every arm except MAPP1's placebo arm, but the FDA finds the data challenging to interpret given variable follow-up and interim treatments.

evidence.locator: 3.2.2.3 Exploratory Efficacy Assessments in Participants from MAPP1 and MAPP2, 2nd paragraph
evidence.extracted: Median time from the last treatment to the follow-up visit 23.4 months (7.9 to 32.4) for MAPP1 participants and 8.5 months (6.0 to 22.8) for MAPP2 participants; some were assessed more than 2 years after the parent study.

evidence.locator: 3.2.2.1 Populations and Baseline Characteristics for MPLONG, 1st paragraph
evidence.extracted: The FDA states that MPLONG, a single assessment 6 months or more after the parent study, was not designed to evaluate durability, that some participants sought other treatments in the interval, and that its results are of very limited value given functional unblinding, about 25% dropout and a single visit after a long and variable interval.
evidence.quote: not properly planned, designed, and implemented to evaluate durability of treatment effect

evidence.extracted: Randomized 91 in MAPP1 and 104 in MAPP2; enrolled in MPLONG 30 of 46 (65.2%) and 30 of 44 (68.2%) treated in MAPP1's MDMA and placebo arms, 45 of 53 (84.9%) and 37 of 51 (72.5%) in MAPP2's; assessed 56 (62% of those randomized in MAPP1) and 81 (78% in MAPP2).

People who enrolled in MPLONG had lower CAPS-5 at their last parent-trial assessment than those who did not: 20.2 (SD 13.2) vs 30.9 (14.1) overall, 15.9 vs 25.4 in the MDMA arms and 24.9 vs 35.8 in the placebo arms; baseline 40.6 vs 43.8.

evidence.locator: 3.2.2.2 Interim Interventions between MAPP1, MAPP2 and MPLONG, 1st to 3rd paragraphs
evidence.extracted: Of 151 people entering MPLONG from MAPP1, MAPP2 or MP16, 75 (82.4%) of those given MDMA and 43 (71.7%) of those given placebo had psychotherapy in the interval; 12 MAPP1 or MAPP2 participants (6 per arm) had ketamine-assisted psychotherapy and one placebo participant 5-MeO-DMT; 13 from the MDMA arms and 7 from the placebo arms reported using MDMA obtained outside the study; unreported use is possible.

FDA tipping-point analysis treating scores after interim ketamine, 5-MeO-DMT or MDMA use as missing (mITT, imputed under missing at random): further change on MDMA from week 18 to the visit -2.02 (95% CI -4.61 to 0.57) in MAPP2 and -4.93 (-9.32 to -0.53) in MAPP1 with no penalty, +0.49 and -1.00 at the largest penalty (20); MAPP2 participants with interim use improved more than those without, which was not seen in MAPP1.

MAPP1 participants were told their allocation before enrolling in MPLONG, MAPP2 participants were not; MPLONG began after MAPP1 ended; the sponsor prespecified no type I error control or estimand for MPLONG, so its results are exploratory, and no missing data were imputed.

evidence.locator: 3.2.3 Efficacy Issues in Detail › Efficacy Issue #1, 8th paragraph (p. 36); Efficacy Issue #2, 3rd, 6th and 9th paragraphs (pp. 37-38)
evidence.extracted: The FDA notes that the difference persisted for at least 6 months and sometimes more than a year and might suggest a true drug effect, but that it is unclear how long expectation bias lasts; time-window analyses showed no meaningful difference between people assessed at 6 to 12 months and later; self-selection may have made the estimate more favourable in either arm, and people who sought further treatment may have had less durable effects.

As corrected, MPLONG enrolled people who had received at least one dose of investigational product, drug or placebo, and its protocol included a review of medical history (not of adverse events), one C-SSRS and one administration of the primary efficacy measure.

evidence.locator: Questions to the Committee, question 1, Committee Discussion
evidence.extracted: On durability, many committee members said there were too many confounders to tease apart in the small data set; members also said functional unblinding and expectation bias may have played a role in the results.
The evaluations did not extend beyond 2 months after therapy; long-term effectiveness depends on an ongoing follow-up (NCT05066282).

evidence.extracted: The primary outcome was a short-term one, 2 months after the last experimental session; long-term follow-up data are to be published later.

risk_of_bias.note: Self-selected attendance by better-off participants, MAPP1 unblinded before the visit, functional unblinding, interim treatments including MDMA from outside the study, single visit at variable times, no prespecified analysis.

inconsistency.note: Both trials' subsets show a persisting difference.

indirectness.note: The claim is limited to the trials' follow-up population and says durability is not established.

imprecision.note: No interval for the between-arm difference at follow-up; subsets of 27 to 44 per arm; the further improvement on MDMA loses significance in a sensitivity analysis.

large_effect.note: Not applicable: the comparison is not protected by randomization at follow-up.

grade.reasoning: MPLONG is an observational study (as the FDA describes it) of self-selected subsets of the randomized arms, so the comparison at follow-up is no longer protected by randomization and is rated as observational evidence, starting low. Risk of bias, one level: those who enrolled had done better by the end of the trials, MAPP1 participants knew their allocation, nearly all participants could tell their allocation anyway, most had other psychotherapy in the interval and some had ketamine or MDMA from outside the study, the visit came at times ranging from 6 to 32 months, and nothing was prespecified. Imprecision, one level: the FDA gives no interval for the between-arm difference at follow-up, the subsets are small, and the further improvement on MDMA is not robust to the FDA's sensitivity analysis. Rated instead as follow-up of randomized arms (starting high), the same problems would need at least three levels of downgrading and the certainty would also be very low. The evidence is seen through the regulator's re-analysis of the sponsor's data; the study report itself was not read. The claim says only that durability is not established, which the evidence shows directly.
